audit.whatIsWrong: 'Ziggs is a 525-range immobile artillery mage with no dash and no escape' (late), echoed in spikes[3] and whys[6] — while the full layer's own cooldown row calls Satchel Charge 'his knockback escape'. The page contradicts itself about whether he can get away.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ziggs flings an explosive charge that detonates after a delay, or when this ability is activated again. The explosion deals magic damage to enemies, knocking them away. Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage.' He has an escape, it is 20/18/16/14/12 seconds, and it reaches 1000 units. For a champion whose only kill pattern is a single committed 500-unit blink, 'he has no escape' is the difference between a guaranteed kill and a wasted Riftwalk on the wrong side of the wave. 'No dash' is fair — a self-knockback is not a dash — but the conclusion drawn from it is not.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge IS his escape: it knocks him clear as well as you, on 20s at rank 1 at 1000 range. He has no dash, but he is only truly catchable once it is spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Inferno Bomb appears nowhere on the page — not in the spikes, not in any why-row, not in the cooldowns block.
audit.why: It is 120/95/70 seconds at 5000 range. Five thousand units means he is a threat to you while you are under your own tower, while you are recalling, and while you are anywhere near an objective — the entire 'just survive the poke and scale' thesis of this page quietly assumes he can only reach you at 850. It is also the reason 'don't let him farm, siege and roam unpunished' matters: the ultimate is his siege tool. Omitting a champion's ultimate from a matchup page is the same class of gap as omitting Vladimir's.
audit.corrected: Mega Inferno Bomb: 120s at rank 1, 5000 range. He taxes you from off-screen, so a spent ultimate is your window to recall or contest an objective.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'you're a blink assassin whose passive already HALVES his only damage type' (late), against '15%' in six other strings on the same page. Also 'your 15% magic resist' in spikes[3], which is the wrong stat.
audit.why: Two different numbers for the same passive on one page, and neither is published by Riot — the description is only 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' 'Halves' is a factor of three away from the figure the rest of the page uses, and it is the sentence that justifies the whole late-game plan. I made it consistent with the page's own 15% rather than introducing a third value, and I corrected 'magic resist' to 'reduction', because Void Stone is flat damage reduction and calling it resist invites the reader to think it stacks with MR the way a resist would.
audit.corrected: Void Stone cuts 15% off his damage — a reduction, not magic resist. One figure, used consistently.

audit.whatIsWrong: Short Fuse is named twice as generic auto-attack poke, with no mention that his own casting accelerates it, and Hexplosive Minefield's diminishing returns are never stated.
audit.why: Riot on Short Fuse: 'Periodically, Ziggs' next basic attack deals bonus magic damage. This cooldown is reduced whenever Ziggs uses an ability.' So the bomb he throws at the wave is also pulling his empowered auto forward — the burst tell is his cast, not his attack timer, which is the flagged autoreset interaction. And Riot on Hexplosive Minefield: 'Successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage', 16 seconds flat at 900 range. That inverts the instinct: if you have to cross the minefield, crossing it fast is cheaper than clipping one mine at a time on the edge, which is exactly the decision you face when blinking in at 6.
audit.corrected: Short Fuse comes back faster every time he casts, so a bomb on the wave means an empowered auto arriving early. And in Hexplosive Minefield (16s, 900 range) each successive detonation on you does less — walk through it rather than skirting it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json (P and E descriptions, E cooldown 16, range 900)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Ziggs levels 1 and 2 at 8/10 — the harshest ratings anywhere in my slice — while the page's own early text says 'At levels 1-2 you're even because his poke is blunted' and whys[1] says the trade 'stays even rather than tilting to him'.
audit.why: The prose is explicit about exactly these two stages, and it gives a coherent mechanical reason: every point of Ziggs' damage is magic, so Void Stone and the Null Sphere shield both apply in full, which is the one matchup profile where a melee mage genuinely holds even against ranged poke. An 8/10 cell sitting above a row that reads 'you're even' is the page arguing with itself in the reader's face. I moved only the two stages the text names, set them to the site's neutral 5/10, and changed win[N] and phases[N] together. Levels 3 and 4-5 have softer language ('drifts back to even', 'dragging the chip war your way') and I left them to Ziggs rather than stretch.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 and 2 are Skill at 5/10. Levels 3 onward unchanged.

audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.why: 58.33% over 12 games. The page quotes no figure. Thin sample, so the chart move above rests on the page's own explicit wording rather than on this number.

edits.before: Ziggs wants to win the early poke war with Bouncing Bomb (Q) and Short Fuse autos, but the whole exchange is magic damage, so Void Stone passively eats 15% of it and Null Sphere (Q) drops a shield that absorbs a full bomb. Don't be bullied by his range: last-hit under tower if you must, take only the trades you can shield, and treat the chip as survivable rather than a problem. At levels 1-2 you're even because his poke is blunted, not because you out-damage him.
edits.after: Ziggs wants to win the early poke war with Bouncing Bomb (850 range, 6s at rank 1) and Short Fuse autos, but every point of it is magic, so Void Stone eats 15% and Null Sphere drops a shield that absorbs a full bomb. Watch the pattern: Short Fuse comes back faster every time he casts, so a bomb thrown at the wave means an empowered auto arriving early. Last-hit under tower if you must, take only the trades you can shield. Levels 1-2 are even because his poke is blunted, not because you out-damage him.

edits.before: From level 3 your Null Sphere shield is on a short enough cooldown to blank a Q-bomb on rotation, and Nether Blade (W) refills your mana on champion hits so you never have to concede the wave to his shove. The lane flips at 6: Riftwalk (R) blinks straight over Hexplosive Minefield (E) and past any Satchel Charge (W) knockback, closing the exact distance his kit is built to hold. Bait the minefield onto the ground, then blink through it onto him.
edits.after: From level 3 your Null Sphere shield is on a short enough cooldown to blank a Q-bomb on rotation, and Nether Blade refills your mana on champion hits so you never concede the wave to his shove. The lane flips at 6: Riftwalk blinks straight over Hexplosive Minefield (16s) and past any Satchel Charge knockback. If you must cross the mines, cross them fast — each successive detonation on you deals less — and count Satchel at 20s at rank 1.

edits.before: This is the matchup you scale for. Ziggs is a 525-range immobile artillery mage with no dash and no escape, and you're a blink assassin whose passive already halves his only damage type. Once Rod of Ages is online and you hit 2+ items, every Riftwalk closes the gap his entire identity depends on keeping, and neither his minefield nor Satchel can save a target that just teleports on top of him. Don't let him farm, siege, and roam unpunished: track his cooldowns, Riftwalk in, and delete him.
edits.after: This is the matchup you scale for. Ziggs is an immobile artillery mage with no dash, and you're a blink assassin whose passive cuts 15% off his only damage type. His one exit is Satchel Charge, which knocks HIM clear as well as you — 20s at rank 1, so count it and commit on the downtime. Mega Inferno Bomb still reaches 5000 units on 120s, so he taxes you from off-screen: track that cooldown, Riftwalk in, and delete him before the siege pays.

notes: Ziggs' ultimate was missing from the page entirely, which is now the third Kassadin matchup in my slice with that problem (Vladimir's Hemoplague and Zaahen's whole kit were the others) — a script comparing each page's text against the packet's enemyAbilities R slot would find the rest cheaply. Two internal contradictions worth noting beyond the edits: the page called Void Stone a 15% reduction in six strings and 'halves' in a seventh, and it called Ziggs escapeless in three strings while the full layer's cooldown row simultaneously described Satchel Charge as 'his knockback escape'. Satchel Charge also carries a percentHealth derived flag in the kit file; Riot's description only attaches percent-health behaviour to hexploding turrets, so I did not write it as percent-health damage against champions.
